title: Blind particle-toss cannot build the human body — or the universe
source_text: XLI. His adde, quod in mentem hominis cadere non potest, corpuscula quaedam varie jactata, absque ullo proposito fine, & absque ullo motore dirigente, potuisse componere tam mirabilem universi structuram, ubi tantus ordo, tanta sapientia, tanta partium omnium consensio & harmonia, quae per tot saecula constans & invariabilis manet, a quovis non omnino caeco animo animadverti potest. Imo si solum hominis corpus consideremus, non puto ullum esse tam stupidum, aut furiosum, qui sibi ipsi persuadere possit, tam mirandam fabricam, in qua tot organa numerari possunt, tam artificiose & concinne fabrefacta, tam apte disposita, ad usus tam varios & multiplices inservientia, fabricam, inquam, hujusmodi non aliam habere causam, quam caecam particularum materiae jactationem.
pass_a_gloss: Add this also, that it cannot fall into the mind of a man that certain corpuscles variously tossed, without any proposed end, and without any directing mover, could have composed so marvelous a structure of the universe, where so great an order, so great a wisdom, so great a consent and harmony of all parts, which through so many ages remains constant and invariable, can be noticed by anyone not altogether blind in mind. Indeed if we considered only the body of a man, I do not think anyone is so stupid, or mad, who could persuade himself that so marvelous a fabric, in which so many organs can be numbered, so artfully and neatly wrought, so aptly disposed, serving such various and manifold uses — a fabric, I say, of this sort — has no other cause than a blind tossing of the particles of matter.
pass_b_english: No sober mind credits ordered universe-harmony to undirected particle-toss.
Even one human body — organs apt for many uses — bars that cause.
Blind matter-jactation cannot build this fabric.
